claims.claim: Severian was Bishop of Gabala in Syria.
Severian flourished from around 400 until 404 as a popular preacher in Constantinople.
Severian was born in the 4th century and died after 408.
Severian spoke Greek with a pronounced Syrian accent.
De caeco nato was formerly attributed to John Chrysostom as author.
De caeco nato survives in manuscripts including Oxford, Bodleian Library, Auct. E. 3. 09 and Oxford, New College, Mss. 082.
The work is also transmitted as part of a longer recension titled De caeco, latrone et fide.
Severian became the enemy of John Chrysostom and helped condemn him at the Synod of the Oak.
Severian was regarded by his contemporaries as a good preacher and author of Biblical commentaries and sermons.
SCOPE: this English is De caeco nato, the sermon stored for severianus-de-caeco-nato. His sermons on Job are a different book.
